name: Bohuslav Enyinnaya-Čermák
role: Mechanic and small-vehicle repair specialist, runs a ground-floor shop in Geartown
location: Geartown — Axle Street, Unit 9, street level beneath the Pembrook residential overhang, near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Bohuslav Enyinnaya-Čermák is a large man gone slightly soft around the middle, with the forearms of someone who has spent three decades using them as his primary tools. His heritage is Czech-Igbo — his father was a machinist from Brno who ended up in Meridian via the Eastern European labor migration of the 2140s, his mother from a Lagos extended family that had been in the city since before it incorporated as Meridian. His face is broad and dark, his hair steel-grey and clipped short, his hands permanently black at the knuckle creases in a way that soap no longer fully addresses. He has a retractable reinforced thumb claw on the right hand — a modification he made himself from salvage parts in 2181 — which he uses as a pry tool so often he's forgotten he has it. His left eye is a secondhand optic he bought from a Geartown parts dealer a decade ago; it's slightly the wrong shade of brown for the natural right eye, which he considers funny.

He is gruff in the manner of someone who has given up pretending to be approachable because being approachable kept leading to people asking him for favors he didn't want to refuse. Underneath the grime and the monosyllables, he is fair to a fault and quietly contemptuous of anyone who isn't. He has an E.L.F. shrine built into the wall above his diagnostic terminal — a gutted engine block filled with machine oil, spare bolts, and a photograph of the first vehicle he ever repaired — dedicated to what he calls the Grease Ghost, a mechanical spirit he credits with keeping the worst jobs manageable. He argues with it sometimes.

core_fears: The shop failing — not financially, but becoming irrelevant as vehicle tech moves beyond his knowledge
His son, who left for a Tessera contract position, becoming someone he doesn't recognize
core_desires: To fix things that matter to people, not just things that are expensive
For the Geartown block to survive the next wave of corporate rezoning
coping_mechanisms: Working through problems physically — when emotionally troubled he finds something to disassemble
The E.L.F. shrine practice, which he would deny is spiritual if pressed
blind_spots: Reads stoicism as strength in others; misses when people around him are struggling
Distrusts institutional solutions so thoroughly he sometimes refuses help that would actually serve him
psychology.secret: He has been quietly cannibalizing a Ferrogate Transit shuttle that was abandoned in an alley behind his shop three years ago. He's not sure if it was stolen, abandoned, or deliberately hidden there, and he has deliberately avoided finding out because the parts are too useful.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Terse, technical, occasionally sardonic; Czech-Igbo idiom blend produces unusual metaphors
speech_patterns.cadence: Short declarative sentences; long technical explanations delivered with total authority and zero concession to jargon
verbal_tics: 'Yes or no?' (used to cut off unnecessary conversation)
example_lines: 'What's wrong with it? You tell me what's wrong, I'll tell you if you're right. Start with what you heard, not what you think.'
'The Grease Ghost was quiet this morning. Either everything's fine or something's about to cost you significantly.'

story_hooks: The Ferrogate shuttle hidden in his alley turns out to have something still inside it — cargo, equipment, or a person — that someone is now looking for
His son contacts him from a Tessera facility with a request Bohuslav can't fulfill without knowing things he's been careful not to know
narrative_function: Reliable resource character — can repair, modify, or assess almost any ground vehicle or mechanical system. Access to Geartown's informal information network. Potential fence for mechanical components, willing or otherwise.
augmentations: Salvage-built retractable reinforced thumb claw, right hand. Secondhand replacement optic, left eye (brown, slightly wrong shade). Subdermal vibration sensor in both palms — lets him diagnose engine problems by feel.
daily_life: Opens at seven, closes when the job is done, which is sometimes midnight. Eats lunch from a noodle cart two doors down, the same cart every day. Argues with the Grease Ghost shrine on bad days. Drinks one beer at the Ferment Quarter on Friday nights, home by ten.
affiliation: Independent; Geartown Mechanics Guild (dues-paying member, rarely attends meetings)

decision_rules: Fix what can be fixed, price it fairly, don't overreach
Never work on something without knowing what it actually does — refuses jobs from clients who won't explain the vehicle's purpose
escalation_ladder: Physically removing the vehicle from the premises and billing for the diagnostic

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assessess competence first, character second; treats proven competence with immediate respect regardless of other factors
interpersonal_modes.friends: Still gruff but shows up, fixes things without being asked, occasionally leaves food at people's doors

stress_responses.low: Works in silence, no music, just the sounds of the shop
stress_responses.medium: Argues with the shrine, then gets back to work
stress_responses.high: Refuses all clients for a day, does inventory alone, emerges with a decision made

contradictions: Insists the E.L.F. shrine is a joke and yet maintains it with genuine care and addresses the Grease Ghost in private
habits: Wipes his hands before speaking to a client even when they won't get clean
Checks the alley behind the shop every morning before opening
breaking_points: Being asked to do something that will harm someone who trusted him with their vehicle

timeline.event: Born in Geartown to Ondřej Čermák and Adaeze Enyinnaya-Čermák
Began working in the shop at 18 under his father
Took over the shop when his father's hands gave out from joint degradation
Son Kelechi accepted a Tessera contract, relocated from Geartown

related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.build: Large-framed, broad-shouldered, gone soft at the belly and flanks after fifty — the physique of someone whose strength was built in his thirties and has slowly traded muscle for weight. Forearms remain thick and corded, built from three decades of wrenching.
physical_description.hair_style: Clipped short, no-nonsense cut. Receding slightly at the temples.
physical_description.eye_color: Right eye: dark brown, natural. Left eye: brown optic, marginally lighter shade, slightly mismatched — a secondhand unit bought from a parts dealer circa 2216.
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep brown, even tone reflecting his mother's Nigerian heritage, weathered by decades of shop work under industrial lighting.
physical_description.complexion: Broad, weathered face. Deep-set eyes. Strong jaw. Permanent creases around the mouth from squinting. Hands permanently stained black at knuckle creases and nail beds — a discoloration that soap no longer fully removes after thirty years of engine work.
distinguishing_marks: Retractable reinforced thumb claw, right hand, salvage-built from scrap parts in 2181 — chrome-edged, used so often he forgets it's augmented. Retracts flush when not in use.
Burn scar along the back of his left forearm, pale and smooth, approximately 8cm long — from a coolant leak in 2189 that he still doesn't talk about.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Retractable reinforced thumb claw on right hand (visible when extended, otherwise flush with palm). Left eye optic: visible only in certain light as a slight mismatch in iris hue and corneal refraction. Subdermal vibration sensor in both palms is not visible but sometimes causes him to press his hands flat against engine blocks in diagnostic poses that look ritualistic.
physical_description.posture_movement: Slouched, economy of motion. Walks with weight on the balls of his feet despite his size — an old mechanic's habit. Hands are always busy or at rest, rarely in between. Rarely makes eye contact, but when he does it's direct and unflinching. When concentrating, he squints with his right eye and tilts his head slightly left, as if his augmented left eye feeds data that requires physical adjustment to interpret.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working class, practical and worn. Heavy grey Kevlar-weave work coveralls with the sleeves rolled to the elbow, revealing forearm tattoos and burn scars. Canvas work boots, resoled twice. A faded teal company shirt from a defunct vehicle manufacturer underneath, visible at the collar. On cold days, a black synthetic-leather jacket that's cracked at the elbows. He wears a brass ring on his left index finger — his father's, from Brno — and a leather cord around his neck with a small chrono-chip for clocking jobs, though he never actually uses it. No jewelry beyond these.
